finding.title: Replace awaited per-row insert/update loops with Drift batch() in curriculum_scope_dao, stage_dao, and track_dao.purgeHistory

evidence.quote:
for (final value in scopeValues) {
        await into(curriculumScopes).insert(

for (final stage in stages) {
        await insertStageDefinition(stage);

for (final stage in stages) {
        await insertStageDefinition(stage);

finding.why: These four loops are all already inside a db.transaction() (so DB-2 is satisfied — no partial-write risk), but each issues N sequential awaited statements where Drift's batch() would send one. track_dao.purgeHistory is the worst case: on 'delete and wipe history' for a track with hundreds of completions, it round-trips once per row to stamp purgedAt instead of one batched UPDATE. The three sites from the companion DB-2 finding (point_config_dao.seedDefaults, study_day_config_dao.seedDefaults, track_learning_order_dao.upsertOrder) share the identical pattern and compound this once they're wrapped in a transaction.
finding.recommendation: Convert each loop to `batch((b) { for (...) { b.insert(...)/b.update(...); } })`, which Drift supports for both inserts and per-row updates with distinct WHERE clauses inside one batch call.
acceptance_criteria: curriculum_scope_dao.setScopes, stage_dao.replaceStagesForTrack/replaceStagesForCurriculum, and track_dao.purgeHistory's tombstone step use batch() instead of a per-row await loop.
Existing tests for these methods pass unchanged (behavior-preserving refactor).

finding.title: Fix hand-rolled test _FakeMergeStore.remoteIsNewer implementations to match DriftMergeStore's clock-skew/D15 semantics

evidence.quote:
// Mirror DriftMergeStore semantics: strict `remote > local` outside
    // the ±5 s window; inside the window, server timestamp decides.

finding.why: mergers_test.dart's fake claims to 'Mirror DriftMergeStore semantics' but omits the D15 fallback (drift_merge_store.dart:140-146): inside the clock-skew window with no decisive synced_at on both sides, the fake unconditionally prefers remote, whereas the real store first falls back to comparing raw updated_at (protecting a newer un-pushed local edit from being clobbered by an older remote). notification_settings_merger_round_trip_test.dart's fake is simpler still — no clock-skew window at all. Neither test currently uses timestamps close enough to trigger the divergent branch, so the suite passes today, but any future near-tie/clock-skew test added against these fakes would silently validate the WRONG (pre-D15) behavior, hiding exactly the bug class DriftMergeStoreTest exists to pin down.
finding.recommendation: Replace both hand-rolled remoteIsNewer bodies with a delegate to the real DriftMergeStore.remoteIsNewer (construct a throwaway DriftMergeStore over an in-memory DB inside the fake, or extract the pure comparison so both share one implementation) instead of re-deriving the algorithm by hand.
acceptance_criteria: A within-skew-window / no-syncedAt / older-remote test case added to either file fails before the fix and passes after, or the fake is proven identical to DriftMergeStore.remoteIsNewer by delegation (making such drift structurally impossible).

finding.title: Centralize app_shell.dart / persistent_switcher_scaffold.dart color literals into AppTheme instead of scattering/duplicating hex values

evidence.quote: const barBackground = Color(0xFFF1F3FA); // opaque pale blue

finding.why: app_shell.dart has 8 raw Color(0x...) literals and persistent_switcher_scaffold.dart has 1 more — all outside lib/core/theme/, exactly what the (currently non-functional, custom_lint is broken repo-wide) no_color_literal_outside_theme rule targets. Worse, the SAME hex value (0xFFF1F3FA, 'opaque pale blue') is hand-copied in both files as an unrelated local constant rather than a shared AppTheme token, and 0xFF0038A8 is a bespoke blue never defined in AppTheme at all (AppTheme.brandBlueDeep is a different value, 0xFF3F41AB). The file's own comments document this exact bar going through TWO rounds of contrast bugs ('Bug 7' and 'Bug 7 (re-fix)') — duplicated, untracked magic colors are precisely what makes a third recurrence likely, since a future contrast fix to one copy can silently miss the other.
finding.recommendation: Move _tutorAccentColor, _childViewAccentColor, barBackground/barBorder, and the nav-item selected-color into AppTheme/AppColors named constants; have persistent_switcher_scaffold.dart reference the same constant app_shell.dart uses.
acceptance_criteria: All Color(0x...) literals in app_shell.dart and persistent_switcher_scaffold.dart are replaced with AppTheme/AppColors named constants.
Once custom_lint's analyzer-version incompatibility is fixed, `dart run custom_lint` reports zero no_color_literal_outside_theme violations in these two files.
0xFFF1F3FA exists as exactly one named constant referenced from both files.

finding.title: Cancel or document the leaked DNS-lookup Future in ConnectivityGateway.isOnline on timeout
finding.rule: Nygard lens — what happens when I/O fails halfway
finding.why: Future.timeout() races a Timer against the lookup but cannot cancel the underlying OS-level DNS resolution — dart:io gives no cancellable primitive for InternetAddress.lookup. Under packet loss or a captive portal (exactly when this check matters most), the original lookup keeps running past the 2s timeout with no way to observe or cancel it; repeated calls (e.g. retrying a failed offline-account conversion in account_actions.dart) can accumulate abandoned lookups.
finding.recommendation: Either document the accepted tradeoff inline (dart:io has no cancellable DNS API) with a bounded-impact justification, or switch to a primitive that supports cancellation (e.g. a raw socket connect with explicit close on timeout).
acceptance_criteria: Either an inline comment documents the accepted leak and its bound, or a test demonstrates no more than one lookup stays in flight after repeated rapid isOnline calls under a simulated timeout
